transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (StellarBridge CTO), Priya Menon (Platform Eng), Eli Turner (Security), Hana Ghosh (PM)

Summary (auto):
Quick sync to align on integrating Redwood as the LLM gateway for StellarBridge marketplace listing and joint ref-arch. Covered VPC peering options, KMS key flow, quantization tradeoffs, and canary rollout. Agreed next steps around benchmarks, diagrams, and a joint ref-arch doc.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started. Quick roll call, I think we have everyone?
[00:06] Daniel Ortiz: Yep, Daniel here.
[00:08] Priya Menon: Priya here.
[00:09] Eli Turner: Eli on security.
[00:11] Hana Ghosh: Hana here.
[00:13] Alex Rivera: Awesome. So objective today is one, align on the integration pattern for StellarBridge marketplace so your customers can opt into Redwood-hosted inference behind your marketplace gateway; two, call out networking/KMS and what we need for a listing; and three, go over perf tradeoffs for quantization and dedicated vs hosted routing.
[00:28] Daniel Ortiz: Cool, thank you. We're primarily focused on two flows: the marketplace-managed hosted path where StellarBridge handles billing and the private path where enterprise buyers want VPC to VPC and their own keys. We need to make sure Redwood's offering fits both.
[00:45] Sofia Patel: Right, and from Redwood's side we support both patterns: hosted API with tenant isolation and Dedicated/Private (VPC) deployments. For listing it'll be important to specify whether it's a SaaS-proxy model or a direct listed endpoint. I'm gonna sketch both.
[01:03] Priya Menon: Quick q — for VPC path, how does auth work? Do we do per-customer role or service account? Also how does KMS integrate?
[01:12] Maya Chen: Great q. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS or redwood-managed KMS depending on your compliance posture. For the marketplace we usually recommend a managed integration where StellarBridge's buyer flow exchanges a short-lived token and Redwood maps it to a customer namespace; for true customer-owned keys you would enable a VPC connector and KMS key policy.
[01:36] Eli Turner: When you say key policy, can you define the key access pattern? We need to make sure we can audit who decrypts. SOC2 scopes require that.
[01:44] Sofia Patel: Practically we add an audit log entry per inference request that references the key id used. If the key is customer-managed in their AWS account, we never see plaintext material; we only get an envelope decryption via the customer's KMS. For audit you get CloudTrail entries on your side and Redwood produces a correlated request log with key id. There's a small caveat on cross-account CloudTrail if logging aggregations are required.
[02:06] Eli Turner: Okay that works, we'll send our compliance matrix.
[02:11] Hana Ghosh: On the marketplace listing checklist, what are the gating items we need to show to the listing team?
[02:18] Maya Chen: Typical items: network connectivity story (VPC peering or private link), KMS and key handling, SSO/SCIM for admin console access, SLA and latency profiles, and a UAT plan for canary. We'll provide a template.
[02:33] Daniel Ortiz: For latency, our buyers care about 95th pct under 250ms for short prompts. Is that realistic?
[02:41] Sofia Patel: For a 2k-context model on optimized infra, hosted latency can be sub-200ms token latency in best-case but depends on batching and cold-start. If customers need strict p95 < 250ms for full-generation flows we often recommend Dedicated placement (reserved capacity) or a hybrid routing policy that pins hot customers to dedicated pools. Also quantization has big benefits.
[03:03] Priya Menon: Can you expand on the quant tradeoffs? We looked at int8 and 4-bit options in the doc but not full ops.
[03:11] Sofia Patel: Sure, quick layman: int8/4-bit quantization reduces memory bandwidth and improves throughput; but for some SFT/fine-tuned models you may see small quality regressions. We have pre-computed quality deltas per model and can suggest a quant profile per workload. For marketplace listing we recommend publishing the recommended quant profile and a quality regression badge in the listing so customers know tradeoffs.
[03:38] Daniel Ortiz: Interesting — we want to surface that to buyers. Could we show an A/B or canary test in the listing so enterprise buyers can request the high-accuracy path?
[03:48] Alex Rivera: Totally. You could have two SKUs in the listing: "standard" (quantized, lower cost) and "premium" (higher-precision model on dedicated). The Redwood routing layer supports SKU-based routing and fallback to avoid timeouts.
[04:01] Hana Ghosh: On billing, how does metering work? We need to reconcile between StellarBridge billing and Redwood usage so our marketplace handles payouts.
[04:09] Maya Chen: We emit per-request metering events with token counts and model id. For marketplace integration we can send a daily CSV or push events to a webhook so you can ingest usage. There's also a marketplace billing connector we use for a few partners.
[04:23] Daniel Ortiz: Is that connector multi-tenant safe?
[04:27] Sofia Patel: Yes, token-level tenant id is included. You control payout mapping. We'll provide sample payloads.
[04:33] [05:00] (background: brief cross-talk about doc links)
[05:08] Priya Menon: For the VPC peering path, network egress — do you expect us to open specific SGs or will Redwood init egress?
[05:15] Alex Rivera: Usually StellarBridge would open inbound from Redwood's egress CIDRs or we set up an AWS PrivateLink endpoint. PrivateLink is cleaner for marketplace traffic and avoids egress IP churn. We'll include both options in the network diagram.
[05:29] Eli Turner: Also want to know about telemetry — can we get traces for latency breakdown from gateway -> redwood -> model?
[05:36] Sofia Patel: Yes we provide distributed tracing headers and per-request spans in the console. You can ingest traces into your APM or use our export to a tracing backend. Note: for Private deployments tracing stays internal to customer's network.
[05:49] Daniel Ortiz: Ok, about canary rollouts — what's a safe pattern? We need to test with a subset of buyers without breaking current flows.
[05:56] Maya Chen: Canary pattern: route a small percentage of traffic to Redwood-hosted model, monitor quality/regressions vs prompt set, then expand. We'll propose a canary config: 2% for 24h, 10% for 48h, 100% when metrics stable. Also we support prompt-anchored evals so we can detect quality drift on key prompts.
[06:17] Hana Ghosh: Will you run an eval against our prompt set as part of POC?
[06:21] Sofia Patel: Yep, that's in scope for the perf POC. We'll need a representative prompt corpus and expected outputs. Priya, can you share a redacted sample?
[06:29] Priya Menon: Yes, will share a 200-prompt set. Some will be >4k tokens.
[06:33] Alex Rivera: Note on very long contexts: runtime selection matters---we may select kernel paths optimized for long sequence; also consider KV caching and prefix caching to reduce cost.
[06:43] Daniel Ortiz: Can you explain prefix/KV cache in plain terms?
[06:46] Sofia Patel: Sure, prefix caching stores repeated instruction/context so it doesn't get reprocessed per request; KV cache stores intermediate attention keys so for multi-turn chats you avoid recomputing past tokens. For marketplace LLM gateway where many buyers share similar system prompts, we can save a lot.
[07:03] Eli Turner: On data retention, can we configure request logs retention? We need minimal retention for compliance.
[07:09] Maya Chen: Yes retention is configurable per-account and we can offer no-logs options for enterprise customers in Private deployments. For hosted marketplace flows we recommend a 30-day default with ability to shorten.
[07:20] Priya Menon: A security nit — for webhook metering, can we sign payloads?
[07:24] Sofia Patel: Absolutely, we HMAC sign all meter webhooks and can set rotating secrets.
[07:29] [08:00] (brief pause while Alex uploads a diagram link)
[08:11] Alex Rivera: Sending the initial reference diagram in chat — it's a rough sketch, please flag errors.
[08:16] Daniel Ortiz: Got it. Looks like you drew both Private and Hosted flows. I see where the KMS arrow is. Who owns the KMS in the Hosted model?
[08:24] Maya Chen: In Hosted, Redwood manages an app-level envelope key but you can opt into bringing your own key for encryption at rest. For request-level encryption we rely on TLS and per-tenant envelopes.
[08:36] Hana Ghosh: For the marketplace listing metadata, can you provide the recommended SLA and typical throughput numbers for the verified models?
[08:44] Sofia Patel: We'll share a perf profile matrix per model (p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory). For a verified medium-sized model you can expect X tokens/sec on rtx-ln class, but I'll attach a real spreadsheet.
[08:58] Daniel Ortiz: On the subject of legal/procurement, do you have an enterprise contract that supports marketplace escrow or revenue share?
[09:05] Alex Rivera: We have workaround templates we've used with other marketplaces; commercial terms are negotiable. For initial listing we can do referral revenue with a simple SLA addendum. Legal will follow up.
[09:17] Priya Menon: Any pitfalls you've seen in previous marketplace integrations?
[09:22] Maya Chen: The common ones: mismatch on expected latency for gen calls, unclear KMS ownership, and billing reconciliation cadence. Early alignment on metering and a short pilot helps avoid surprises.
[09:33] Eli Turner: We want to run an internal security review; are there docs we can start with?
[09:37] Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll share our security pack (SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, KMS flow, network diagram). We'll also provide sample scim/saml assertion details for admin access.
[09:49] Hana Ghosh: Timeline-wise, we'd like to go to early access in March. Is that feasible?
[09:54] Alex Rivera: Feasible. If we get your prompt corpus and compliance matrix this week/next, Redwood can run the perf POC in Feb and aim for an early access listing in late March.
[10:06] Priya Menon: One more question — fallback behavior when Dedicated pool is saturated.
[10:12] Sofia Patel: Redwood routing supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to hosted pools with a degradation policy. We recommend defining a fallback SLA so buyers know expected behavior.
[10:23] Daniel Ortiz: Good. Let's capture next steps.
[10:27] Alex Rivera: Recap: Alex sends network diagram + latency spreadsheet; Sofia runs quantized perf tests; Maya & Priya draft refarch and marketplace checklist; Eli shares compliance matrix; schedule follow-up for canary/UAT in week of Feb 22.
[10:43] Hana Ghosh: Thanks all.
[10:46] Daniel Ortiz: Appreciate it.
[10:48] Alex Rivera: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the notes.

End transcript.
